event: Daily Intelligence Briefing
title: Daily Market Briefing
text:
BOTTOM LINE — Forced squeeze inside a downtrend.
Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia (+31.48%) lifted Nasdaq futures into a violent snapback after Friday's 5.3% Nasdaq plunge left the S&P 10% off its Oct. 6 high; Nov flash PMIs (Mfg 54.5 in-line, Services 54.7 vs 55.6) confirmed a slowing but non-collapsing economy. Cap it as a positioning unwind, not a trend change: VIX at 35.9 still pins a 52-week high.

INDICES — Fear peaking, not clearing.
VIX 35.9, at its 52-week high (range 13.5–35.9) even as VIX futures fell 12.99%. Ranked: SOXX +13.63%, QQQ +7.00%, SPY +4.71%, IWM +3.56%, DIA +3.06% — large beat small by 3.44pp into mega-cap semis. Biggest cross-asset move: silver +5.25% and gold +3.14% alongside a +0.54% dollar. SPY and QQQ both close below their 200-DMA — CTA sell trigger still live.

VOLUME & BREADTH — Accumulation with a headline distortion.
SPY vol_ratio 1.5x with price +4.71% and QQQ 1.3x-class buying via XLK at 1.6x = genuine accumulation, though QQQ's -$3.17B five-day outflow (6th percentile) shows it is re-loading, not chasing. SOXX 2.1x and IJR 1.6x gaining while IWM, RSP and DIA sit near 1.0–1.1x means the move was concentrated, not broad. Breadth says otherwise: 419/82 advancers, up/down volume 6.40x, but only 52% of the index above its 50/200-DMA and 17 new 60-day lows vs 8 highs — participation diverges from the +4.71% tape.

SECTORS & ROTATION — XLK Technology +8.97%, XLY Discretionary +3.97%, XLI Industrials +3.90%, XLC Comms +3.57%, XLB Materials +3.23%, XLF Financials +1.98%, XLU Utilities +1.48%, XLV Healthcare +1.23%, XLRE Real Estate +1.04%, XLP Staples -0.09%, XLE Energy -1.06%.
SMH +15.03% and DRAM +18.62% topped industries; XOP -1.66% and UNG -6.63% lagged. Flows contradict price: XLC +$280mm (92nd pct) and XLP +$231mm (83rd) led inflows while XLE bled -$1.14B (2nd pct) and XLV -$884mm (2nd), yet the top price sector drew net ETF selling (SOXX -$3.58B). Money is buying defensives and selling energy/healthcare — the opposite of today's tape. Label: AI hardware leading, on short-covering rather than conviction.

POSITIONING — Protection still bid despite the rip.
SPY PCR 0.98 and QQQ 0.71 sit in neutral-complacent territory, but skew is +16.2%/+17.0% (put premium) with SPY IV 25.9% and QQQ 37.4%. VIX 35.9 is 65% above its 21.7 20-day MA, and QQQ spot sits versus a 677 gamma flip — a break lower re-accelerates dealer selling. VIXEQ 49.1 vs VIX 35.9 is a 13-point gap: high single-stock dispersion, a rotation tape, not a macro one.

CROSS-ASSET — Commodities and semis telling different stories.
USO -4.49% and UNG -6.63% extended oil’s 20-day -19.77% slide even as equities ripped — a demand signal the equity rally ignores; silver’s +5.25% with a firm dollar is the real tension. Next FOMC: Dec 9, 2026; Polymarket prices 94% for a 25bp HIKE (up +2pp in 5 days), only 3% for no change — the market is pricing tightening into this rally.

SIGNALS & WATCH — 46.8, Neutral.
Top movers: NVDA +31.48% (Huang reinstated as CEO), MU +19.04%, MRVL +18.37% (headline noted no company-specific news). Vol spikes: NVDA 2.8x and QQQE 3.5x at +4.94% — accumulation, but QQQE’s equal-weight semi bid diverges from only 52% of S&P names above their 50-DMA. Momentum extremes: XLK best 20-day -12.85%, XLE worst -14.03%. Watch into tomorrow’s Consumer Confidence (fc 92.5) and Wednesday’s Core PCE (fc 3.2% y/y): UUP +0.54%, SOXX +13.63%, and XLE -1.06% each sit at a decision point against the semis-led squeeze.
